articles.title: Eleven Trans-Neptunian Objects and Eight Candidates Discovered by TESS
articles.summary: We report a blind search for trans-Neptunian objects (TNOs) in Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) full-frame images from 2018 July 25 through 2026 November 6. We search 572 CCD fields near the ecliptic across 95 TESS sectors. After modeling and subtracting Gaia stars with the TESS-Gaia Light Curve package, we stack the residuals along curved trial paths and link detections across sectors. articles.title: The effect of vertical mixing on oxygen sequestration by refractory elements in the atmosphere of giant planets

articles.summary: Collisionless shocks are primary sites of particle acceleration throughout the Universe. articles.title: JCMT--Venus: Daily Monitoring of HDO and SO$_2$ Absorption in Venus' Mesosphere
articles.summary: We present three multi-week, disc-integrated James Clerk Maxwell Telescope (JCMT) campaigns monitoring HDO and SO$_2$ absorption in Venus' upper mesosphere at altitudes of approximately 80--110 km. articles.summary: Auroral variability in ultracool dwarfs (UCDs) has been proposed as a key source of optical and infrared modulation, yet its physical origin remains poorly understood. We present JWST Near Infrared Imager and Slitless Spectrograph/Single Object Slitless Spectroscopy (NIRISS/SOSS) time-series spectroscopy of the M8.5 UCD LSR J1835+3259. articles.title: A helium-rich mass-donor in a 3.5-hr low mass X-ray binary
articles.summary: Binary systems in which a neutron star accretes material from a low-mass stellar companion arise from evolutionary processes that depend sensitively on the progenitor properties. articles.title: Discovery of a Short-Duration Fast X-ray Transient Associated with a Short Gamma-Ray Burst
articles.summary: Extragalactic fast X-ray transients (EFXTs) are an emerging population of high-energy transients with diverse physical origins. articles.title: Constraining Accretion Regimes of Little Red Dots from Their Variability

articles.summary: Numerical relativity simulations of binary neutron star mergers and core-collapse supernovae indicate that the neutron star matter can be driven far from equilibrium due to large amplitude density oscillations, with frequency in the kHz range. articles.summary: The Ariel mission will conduct a population-level survey of approximately 1000 exoplanet atmospheres across its nominal lifetime, requiring unprecedented consistency in the treatment of stellar contamination of transmission spectra. articles.summary: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are millisecond-duration radio transients of extragalactic origin. articles.title: JWST Rocky Worlds DDT Observations of LTT 1445 A b and c in Secondary Eclipse Using MIRI/F1500W
articles.summary: The JWST Rocky Worlds Director's Discretionary Time (RWDDT) program uses secondary eclipse observations to determine the conditions under which rocky exoplanets around M dwarfs retain their atmospheres. articles.title: The origin of Potassium in Galactic chemical evolution - The effect of C-O shell mergers in massive stars
articles.summary: The Galactic chemical evolution (GCE) of potassium (K) and of most other odd-Z elements remains poorly understood: models generally underproduce the observed [K/Fe] over a wide metallicity range, depending on the adopted massive star yields. A proposed site for efficient K nucleosynthesis is the merger between the oxygen and carbon shells (C-O shell merger) that can occur in massive stars a few hours before core collapse. articles.summary: Continuous gravitational waves (CWs) from neutron stars beyond the Galactic Center can be lensed by the supermassive black hole in Sgr A$^*$. articles.summary: Compact millimeter emission from radio-quiet active galactic nuclei has been proposed as a probe of magnetized accretion-disk coronae. articles.title: Lurkers at the Threshold: GWTC-4.0's near-threshold events

articles.title: Stellar-Field-Driven Induction Heating Unlikely To Cause Significant Heating in Giant Exoplanets
articles.summary: A planet moving through a changing magnetic field will have a current induced on it by that magnetic field. If the magnetic Reynolds number in the upper atmosphere of this planet is small, the dissipation of this current could result in observable changes to the planet's properties. In this paper, we estimated the total power that would be dissipated in the observed giant exoplanet population if they orbited stars with misaligned magnetic dipoles. articles.title: Lense-Thirring induced repeating blast trains in continuous gravitational waves
articles.summary: We characterise gravitational lensing induced by the Lense-Thirring effect in a continuous gravitational-wave source orbiting a spinning supermassive black hole. articles.title: Bayesian Inference of Fermionic Dark Matter Admixed Neutron Stars Informed by Galaxy Cluster Constraints

articles.title: The Same But Different: SiO$_2$ Clouds in Two L-Dwarfs with JWST

articles.summary: The origins and architectures of hot Jupiter (HJ) systems remain unclear, with potential explanations for the tight orbits being in-situ formation, disk-migration, or high-eccentricity migration. articles.summary: We present a global fit to geo-neutrino measurements at four underground sites (Kamioka, Gran Sasso, Sudbury, Jiangmen), combining signal rates with site-specific predictions of the lithospheric contribution to constrain the quantity and distribution of radioactivity in the Earth's mantle. articles.summary: Standard siren cosmology depends on several modelling assumptions, including the underlying source population, galaxy catalogue, and detection selection function. As gravitational-wave catalogs grow incrementally, much computational effort is spent re-analysing largely overlapping datasets. articles.title: Nucleation of water ice under weak ionization via clustering on negative ions
articles.summary: Water-ice grains are shown to form spontaneously in a cold, weakly-ionized laboratory plasma with trace water admixture when neutrals and ions are cooled below $\sim$200 K. articles.title: Analysis Methodology of the Search for Ultrahigh Energy Neutrinos in 10.6 Years of Askaryan Radio Array Data
articles.summary: The Askaryan Radio Array (ARA) is an in-ice radio observatory at the South Pole designed to detect ultrahigh energy (UHE) neutrinos through Askaryan emission produced by interactions of neutrinos and their secondary particles. In this paper, we present the detailed methodology of the first array-wide search for a diffuse UHE neutrino flux using data from all five ARA stations. articles.summary: Very-high-energy (VHE, $E \gtrsim 50$\,GeV) $γ$-ray astronomy has evolved into an indispensable pillar of modern astroparticle physics, offering a direct view of non-thermal particle acceleration, cosmic-ray origins, and fundamental physics. articles.summary: LMC X-3 is a persistent black hole high-mass X-ray binary and serves as an important laboratory for studying accretion disk evolution across different spectral states. Using broadband X-ray light curves, hardness diagnostics, power spectral analysis, and spectral modeling, we investigate the long-term evolution of the source across multiple epochs. articles.title: A large radiatively loud anti-glitch in 1E 2259+586 with a protracted recovery
articles.summary: Context. Anti-glitches are rare and enigmatic timing anomalies. High-cadence monitoring has revealed radiatively quiet anti-glitches in several pulsar populations, but radiatively loud anti-glitches and their links to magnetospheric activity remain poorly understood. Aims. We characterize a new, large anti-glitch in the magnetar 1E 2259+586 and compare its phenomenology with other magnetars. Methods. We analyze timing, flux, pulse-profile evolution, and spectra using EP, NICER, and IXPE X-ray observations. Results. articles.title: Empirical constraints on cosmic-ray scattering in NGC 1333 from dust polarisation
articles.summary: Cosmic rays (CRs) regulate molecular-cloud ionization and chemistry. Gyro-resonant scattering by magnetic fluctuations sets their mean free path and, on larger scales, their effective diffusion coefficient. However, coefficients inferred from CR distributions averaged over cloud to Galactic scales leave local magnetic structure unresolved. We use the magnetic-field structure of NGC 1333 and its embedded protostellar core IRAS 4A to estimate local CR scattering rates and effective diffusion coefficients, $D(E)$, and examine their variation with environment and scale. articles.title: Search Method for Continuous Gravitational Waves from Rotating Neutron Stars in Highly Eccentric Wide Orbits
articles.summary: Recent results from the Gaia third data release have highlighted 21 potential neutron stars candidates in wide, highly-eccentric binary systems and provide estimates of their orbital parameters. We present a feasibility study for a directed search for continuous gravitational waves (CWs) tailored for these and similar systems. To this extent, we have computed a frequency metric to place templates in the parameter space accounting for uncertainties on the orbital parameters. articles.title: The Brown Dwarf Desert is a Mass-Ratio Desert: Astrometric Demographics of 63,254 Stars
articles.summary: Brown dwarfs are rare as close companions to stars compared to planets and stellar companions, a paucity known as the brown dwarf desert. Here we apply a novel joint-modelling method to Hipparcos and Gaia DR2/DR3 astrometry from 63,254 stars to complete this picture with a sample 1-2 orders of magnitude larger than those of previous wide-orbit demographic studies. articles.title: Search for a Dispersion Measure Excess Toward Nearby Galaxy Halos Using Fast Radio Bursts from the Second CHIME/FRB Baseband Catalog
articles.summary: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) probe foreground ionized baryons via their dispersion measures (DM). Using 1748 sub-arcminute-localized sources from the Second CHIME/FRB Baseband Catalog, we conduct a statistical stacking study of the circumgalactic media (CGM) of nearby galaxies by analyzing the DMs of FRBs whose sightlines intersect foreground halos. articles.title: The Tierras Observatory: Ultra-Precise Photometry for Characterizing Exoplanets and Their Host Stars
articles.summary: The Tierras Observatory is a fully robotic 1.3-m telescope at the Fred Lawrence Whipple Observatory in southern Arizona. Tierras achieves sub-part-per-thousand (ppt) photometric precision on two timescales: intra-night, to detect and characterize transits of planets around nearby mid-to-late M dwarfs, and night-to-night across an observing season, to characterize the long-term variability of their host stars. articles.title: AGN Feedback Turbulence in Cool-core Clusters: Evidence from XRISM
articles.summary: The XRISM X-ray Observatory has revealed evidence for a "double-cascade" scenario in the Perseus cluster, in which active galactic nucleus (AGN) feedback and mergers drive turbulence over distinct radial ranges and spatial scales. articles.title: Joint Gaia-Hipparcos astrometry, RV, and Imaging posteriors from the G23H Hipparcos sample
articles.summary: We present uniform posteriors indicating the presence or absence of stellar and planetary companions over a sample of $10^5$ stars in Hipparcos and Gaia. articles.title: Numerical-Relativity Particle-in-Cell Simulations: Self-Gravitating Collisionless Matter in Dynamical Spacetimes
articles.summary: Gravitational collapse and instability, black-hole dynamics in systems with large scale separations, and questions surrounding extremal black hole formation require full nonlinear studies using accurate and adapted numerical tools. articles.title: Simulation of a Jovian Planet Undergoing Gas Accretion
articles.summary: To understand the process of planet formation in the Solar System or any other stellar system, we need to comprehend the interaction between forming planets and the protoplanetary disk. articles.summary: Several indirect observations imply that the central compact object in the supernova SN 1987A is likely to be the youngest neutron star identified to date, NS 1987A. articles.title: MarsNet: Learning the Martian Atmosphere from Observations Alone
articles.summary: We present MarsNet, a machine-learned model of the Martian atmosphere trained only on observations. Existing reanalyses assimilate spacecraft retrievals into general circulation models (GCMs), so where observations are sparse their fields largely reflect the model. articles.title: GRB 241030A: A fallback-accreting magnetar description of the early X-ray emission
articles.summary: The bright, variable early X-ray emission of GRB~241030A at $z=1.411$ motivates investigating continued central-engine activity before the smoother afterglow emerges.
